title: Frobenius coin analogies
connection: Compare admissible sums of auxiliary parameters with numerical semigroup conductor problems.
why: If a certificate construction is additive in one coordinate, conductor bounds could convert families into eventual coverage.
first_step: For each ES modulus 4C, derive the largest missing admissible divisor residue from small data and seek a semigroup-style conductor bound.
alt_first_steps: [free_astra-0043] Find an exact ansatz with an additive free coordinate before computing its attainable residues and gaps.

repo_status.note: Frobenius-coin analogue for admissible divisor residues not examined.

pass1.summary: Not actionable as stated. Conductor bounds need an additively closed set (a numerical semigroup), and no ES certificate set has that. The word sets {tuv−u−v} are not closed under addition, and the only additive moves (d ↦ d+1 in ET coordinates, n ↦ n+4ab) generate residue classes, i.e. B1 congruence families, not semigroups. 'Largest missing admissible divisor residue mod 4C' is undefined for a fixed modulus, since the target class −1 is fixed and the divisor set is per-integer. The one honest Frobenius echo is already in the repo: t = 1 words uv−u−v are Sylvester's Frobenius numbers g(u,v), and the co-finiteness statement I3 ('every n > 2 433 600 is tuv−u−v with t,u,v ≥ 3', CERTIFIED to 10^9) is the conductor-type statement. A web search found no Frobenius/ES literature link.
evidence: web search 'Erdős-Straus conjecture Frobenius number numerical semigroup' (no hit)

title: Positivstellensatz / SOS degree of infeasibility certificates for bounded ES failures
connection: For bounded parameters, 'no certificate at p up to height B' is a finite infeasibility statement with a Positivstellensatz/SOS (or Nullstellensatz) refutation. The degree needed as a function of p and B is a proof-complexity measure.
why: If refutation degree must grow, low-degree 'algebraic' proofs of existence are impossible in a quantifiable sense (analogue of B1). If it stays bounded for some encoding, that encoding has hidden structure.
first_step: For p failing ES₅ at small B (e.g. p = 5, 13, 17, 2521 for I3_𝒞), compute minimal Nullstellensatz degree over F₂ of the bounded infeasibility system.
alt_first_steps: [upgrades-0174] Encode 'no (★) certificate with u, B, C ≤ X' for a fixed true p as an infeasible polynomial system and compute Nullstellensatz degree for small X.
refs: arXiv:1603.04246 (Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 8)

repo_status.evidence: SOS certificates prove *real* infeasibility or real positivity; ES failures at odd squares are not real-infeasible
repo_status.note: Real-SOS variant collapsed; finite-height Nullstellensatz degree for bounded failures never computed.

pass1.summary: Not actionable as stated: at a true prime, 'no certificate with u,B,C ≤ X' is infeasible only because the box excludes the existing solutions, and over F₂ any infeasible system in n Boolean variables has a Nullstellensatz refutation of degree ≤ n; the measured degree would depend entirely on the chosen bit/carry encoding of 4uBC − u − B = p (a factoring-type circuit), not on ES structure. The real-SOS variant already collapsed (s4_real_analytic_tools.md §3: odd-square failures are not real-infeasible), and the unbounded ES statement has no finite system to refute.

title: Parallel resistors: ES ⇔ a resistance n/4 Ω made from three integer resistors in parallel
connection: Conductances add in parallel: 1/R = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z. So ES ⇔ R = n/4 is a parallel combination of three integer resistors (equivalently three thin lenses of integer focal length in contact).
why: Electrical networks connect to squared rectangles (Brooks–Smith–Stone–Tutte) and Kirchhoff matrix-tree counts; a network-theoretic proof of a 'three-branch' realizability statement is conceivable.
first_step: Check the literature on 'realizing resistance values with k resistors' (series–parallel, minimal number of unit resistors) for 3-branch parallel results.
alt_first_steps: [translate-0030] None beyond item 6 (resistor networks); use as a pedagogical bridge only.

repo_status.note: Parallel-resistor realisation of n/4 not examined in repo.

pass1.summary: Not actionable: 1/R = 1/x+1/y+1/z with R = n/4 is literally the ES equation, a restatement with no new test. Literature check (Eppstein's Egyptian fractions & parallel resistors page) shows only the classical pedagogical identification of unit-fraction sums with parallel resistors; no three-branch realizability result beyond ES itself.

connection: φ(n) | n − 1 implies inequalities and Egyptian-type relations on the prime factors. Another rigid multiplicative/Egyptian sibling with open status.
why: Methods to bound or exclude solutions there might adapt to proving rigidity (non-existence) in constrained ES worlds, i.e. explaining their failure sets.

title: Hilbert's 10th / Diophantine sets: the set of ES-failing n is Diophantine (co-r.e.) — trivial but formal
connection: {n : ¬ES(n)} is Π₁-definable, hence its complement {n : ES(n)} is Diophantine (Σ₁) by MRDP; a polynomial whose positive values are exactly ES-good n exists. Nothing new arithmetically, but gives a 'polynomial certificate world'.
why: Mostly formal; MRDP polynomials are huge. Recorded to close the logic direction.
first_step: Note; skip unless a logician collaborator is interested.

repo_status.note: Diophantine (MRDP) formalization of ES-good set not examined.

pass1.summary: Formal triviality with no ES content: ES(n) is already Sigma_1 by its own definition (exists x,y,z >= 1 with 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx)), so it is Diophantine; a positive-valued polynomial for the set is a standard consequence of MRDP/Jones and adds no arithmetic information. Not a route to a proof; logic framing is already in logic_complexity.

title: McMullen's uniformly diophantine numbers in a fixed quadratic field ↔ periodic HJ data
connection: McMullen showed every real quadratic field contains infinitely many periodic continued fractions with bounded partial quotients. ES words relate to quadratic data via γ_w (trace A + A*). A quadratic-field-uniform statement is a model for 'certificates in every class'.
why: It is one of the rare pointwise CF theorems proved by a non-expansion argument (closed geodesics, Hecke-type operators).
first_step: Read McMullen 'Uniformly Diophantine numbers in a fixed real quadratic field' (Compositio 2009) and check whether its geodesic-construction trick could prescribe a trace/level relation like ES's.
refs: McMullen, Uniformly Diophantine numbers in a fixed real quadratic field (Compos. Math. 2009)

repo_status.note: No repo document examines this connection; catalog listings only.

pass1.summary: Not actionable as stated: McMullen (Compositio 2009) concerns bounded-partial-quotient closed geodesics in a fixed real quadratic field (abstract confirmed by search); ES has no continued-fraction or geodesic variable, so the proposed geodesic-construction trick has no target. The CF/thin-orbit family is already catalogued in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md row 1.

title: Littlewood conjecture / Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss measure rigidity for product approximations
connection: EKL: the exceptional set for Littlewood's conjecture has dimension 0, via measure rigidity of diagonal actions; ES approximates 4/n by sums of unit fractions — a multiplicative Diophantine approximation shape.
why: Diagonal-action rigidity controls simultaneous multiplicative approximations, the structure of 4/n − 1/x ≈ product-type quantities.
first_step: Check whether ES's second step (4/n − 1/x = 1/y + 1/z) can be phrased as a multiplicative approximation problem for a diagonal action.
refs: Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture, Ann. Math. 164 (2006)

repo_status.note: No repo document examines this connection; catalog listings only.

pass1.summary: Not actionable: EKL measure rigidity gives dimension/a.e. statements for real-parameter multiplicative approximation; ES is a single-n integer existence question. The second step 1/y+1/z = (4x-n)/(nx) is a divisor problem, with no diagonal action in sight.

why: A transference principle between simultaneous approximation and congruence choices might provide a useful model for pointwise witness selection.
first_step: Inspect the survey’s reduction to a finite set of simultaneous inequalities; ask whether ES’s divisor-in-residue condition admits a comparable finite approximation statement.

first_step: Read Graham, 'On finite sums of reciprocals of distinct nth powers' (Pacific J. Math 1964) and note whether its method uses a thick reservoir (likely yes).

title: Model theory: is ES expressible in a decidable theory after fixing the structure of (ℕ, +, ·|_{divisors of 4Cp+1})?
connection: Full arithmetic is undecidable, but fragments like Presburger + 'is a power of 2' (Büchi) or Skolem arithmetic (ℕ, ·) are decidable. ES mixes + and · minimally: 4Cp + 1 = ab, a ≡ b ≡ −1 (4C). Determine the weakest theory in which ES is expressible and whether any known decidability/undecidability result applies to its ∀∃ fragment.
why: Calibration: if ES lies in a decidable fragment, there's an algorithm to decide it (in principle); more realistically it identifies ES's logical complexity relative to e.g. Zaremba (also ∀∃ with bounded searches).
first_step: Write ES in the language (ℕ, +, ·, <) and try to reduce the number of multiplications; note that 'a ≡ −1 mod 4C' and 'ab = 4Cp+1' need two products with shared variables; check against the known decidable fragments (e.g. 'one multiplication' theories are already undecidable? — Robinson).
alt_first_steps: [free_opus-0328] Read Lipshitz 'The Diophantine problem for addition and divisibility' and check whether ES(p) (with xyz multiplication eliminated via Type II linearisation) fits into the decidable fragment — and what the decision procedure's 'local-global' principle says.

repo_status.note: No repo document applies this technique or analogy to ES; generic.

pass1.summary: Calibration only: for fixed p, ES(p) is a bounded finite search and so decidable; the uniform statement over p needs variable products (ab = 4Cp+1 with a, b, C, p all varying), outside the Presburger/Buchi fragments. No concrete test was identified.

title: Sperner/Tucker on the level × divisor grid
connection: Sperner's lemma forces a fully-labelled cell in any boundary-respecting labelling. Lay out levels C (one axis) and divisor sizes log d / log N (other axis); label grid cells by the class of the divisor relative to −1 (mod 4C); boundary conditions come from trivial divisors (1 and N always in class 1). A fully-labelled cell would be a certificate.
why: Odd, but Sperner-type lemmas give existence from boundary data alone.
first_step: Construct the labelled grid for small p and check whether natural boundary conditions hold and what a fully-labelled cell means.
alt_first_steps: [free_opus-0313] Define labels on lattice points (x,y) in [p/4, p]² by sign/residue of 4xy − p(x+y) relative to divisibility of the remainder; check whether boundary labels are forced.

repo_status.note: Sperner/Tucker labelling of level×divisor grid not examined.

pass1.summary: Not actionable as stated: the proposed labels (divisor class mod 4C on a level x divisor grid) are not defined on the grid boundary, so no Sperner or Tucker boundary condition is forced, and a fully labelled cell would not be an ES certificate.
